newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to sell-off chemical firm, rose oil plant.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to sell-off chemical firm, rose oil plant.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday stepped up privatisation efforts in line with pledges to multilateral lenders by offering a second chemical firm and a rose-oil distillery.

"The cabinet sanctioned the Privatisation Agency to open a privatisation procedure offering 60 percent of Himko-Vratza," government spokeswoman Lyubov Vidinska told reporters after the cabinet meeting.

The Vratza-based chemical fertiliser producer Himko is the second chemical company after calcinated soda producer Sodi-Devnya to be put on the counter among other 20 major state enterprises which the government hopes to sell by year-end in a bid to raise desperately needed cash.

Earlier this year Himko set up a joint venture with Frankfurt-based Messer Grieshelm GmbH, a subsidiary of Germany's Hoechst, to distribute industrial gases in the region. Himko's net profit for 1994 was 60 million levs.
The sell-off of majority stakes in a further six state companies was also approved by the cabinet on Thursday.
A 72 percent stake in Kazanlak-based rose-oil distillery Balgarska Rosa will also be offered to private investors.
Rose oil distilled into attar of roses, a centuries-old elixir, is exported to perfume houses. Bulgaria produced about 500 kg (1,100 lb) of rose oil last year.

A 72 percent stake in bio-products manufacturer Vetprom in Radomir is offered for sale, along with 26.4 percent in ceramics maker Harmanliiska Keramika, 26.6 percent in electronics producer EAZ-Plovdiv, 14 percent in a dairy processing plant in Plovdiv and 25 percent in Sirma textile maker also in Plovdiv.

The close of business on Thursday is the tender deadline for investors' bids for Sodi Devnya. The envelopes containing the bids will be opened by a commission consisting of several ministers and privatisation agency executives. It is still unclear when the tender results will announced.

Six foreign investors including South Korea's LG Group Belgium's Solvay & Cie, Rhone-Poulenc, and Brunner Mond Plc have shown interest in Sodi Devnya so far, the privatisation agency has said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
